name: v0.16.2
body:
# pdfcpu v0.16.2

Hello!

This release makes PDF workflows more reliable: 
- preserving document content during processing
- improving forms and encrypted PDFs
- handling malformed files more safely.

**Upgrading is highly recommended.** Existing Go API signatures remain unchanged.

Release binaries were built with Go 1.27.2, which includes important security fixes. 
Building requires Go 1.26 or later.

## Highlights

- **Preserve more of your documents.** Fixes retain inherited page boundaries and resources, shared stamp resources,
  catalog data, and named destinations during affected page, merge, stamp, and bookmark operations.

- **Work more reliably with forms.** Improvements cover inherited fields, checkboxes and radio buttons, export ordering,
  JSON field matching, empty list boxes, and Unicode text limits.

- **Improve text and image fidelity.** Fixes address text decoding, font mappings and widths, CMYK image extraction,
  RGBA image import, and compressed image data.

- **Improve encrypted PDF handling.** Corrections cover AES-256 passwords, crypt-filter selection, extraction permissions,
  and encryption of strings rewritten from object streams.

## For Existing Users

- **Validation is more precise.** Strict mode rejects additional malformed inputs. Relaxed mode retains applicable
  compatibility cases and reports notices; it does not bypass every validation or writing requirement.

- **PDF 2.0 output has additional checks.** Writing fails when required annotation appearances are missing. Automatic
  appearance generation remains incomplete. Standard-font metric completion can also report errors for partial metrics
  or unsupported encodings it cannot reconstruct.

- **Extraction permissions are enforced correctly.** Accessibility permission alone no longer authorizes general extraction.

- **AES-256 password preparation is corrected.** Unicode normalization and password-length handling now apply consistently
  when creating and opening encrypted files. Encryption defaults are unchanged.

- **Corrected decoding may change results.** Applications comparing extracted text or image data should review their
  expected output.

## For API Users

- Existing exported function and method signatures, including `pkg/api`, remain unchanged.

- Supporting packages receive additive exports for catalog entries, standard-font metric completion, and annotation
  appearance checks.

- Integrations should account for the behavior changes above, particularly stricter validation, corrected extraction
  permissions, and PDF 2.0 write errors.

## Fixed Security Advisories

- **[GHSA-ppm7-rg95-2c2p — Plaintext strings in encrypted PDFs](https://github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu/security/advisories/GHSA-ppm7-rg95-2c2p)**
  When encrypting PDFs containing object streams, some strings could remain readable without a password despite the
  operation completing successfully. Affects versions **v0.8.0 through v0.16.1**.

- **[GHSA-gj7c-wpph-xx35 — Process termination from recursive stream references](https://github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu/security/advisories/GHSA-gj7c-wpph-xx35)**
  Malformed PDFs with circular `/Filter` or `/DecodeParms` references could cause a fatal stack overflow. v0.16.2 detects
  these references and returns an error. Affects Go module versions **v0.2.3 through v0.16.1**; older repository releases
  are also affected.

If an affected version was used to encrypt PDFs containing object streams, review the
output for exposed sensitive material and regenerate it from a trusted source. 
Upgrading does not repair files already produced.

## Reliability and Security

- Bound excessive parsing work, reject circular stream-filter references, and enforce resource limits during decoding
  and cross-reference repair.

- Prevent malformed-input panics involving object streams, cross-reference data, colour spaces, and annotations.

- Correct PDF whitespace handling, inline-image parsing, effective-version detection, and damaged-file recovery.

- Strengthen validation across images, graphics, destinations, page labels, and PDF 2.0 entries while restoring targeted
  multimedia compatibility.

- Expand regression coverage for encryption, document preservation, forms, parsing, images, fonts, and validation.

## Internals and Performance

- Reuse validation results for shared JavaScript, Web Capture, 3D, RichMedia, and Rendition objects, reducing repeated
  work while retaining cancellation and cycle checks.

- Reduce allocation overhead when parsing large certificate revocation lists. Regression tests check preservation of
  revocation entries and signatures and bound allocation counts.

## Thanks

Thanks to everyone who reported issues and helped improve pdfcpu.

Special thanks to @qoke and the IQ Hive team for contributing the substantial set of fixes behind this release.
